title: Subtask generation as a branching process: critical cleanup ratio

hypothesis.statement: When every executed job spawns m children on average and a fraction d is cancelled before running, work per root job is 1/(1 - m(1-d)) below m_ef = m(1-d) = 1 and unbounded at or above it; the transition is abrupt, the minimum cleanup is d* = 1 - 1/m, and a hard depth limit bounds the work at a cost that grows geometrically with the depth.

predictions.text: Subcritical, no cleanup: for m = 0.8, 0.9 and 0.95 the mean number of executed jobs per root is within 3% of 1/(1-m) (5, 10, 20) and no root reaches the 20,000-job cap.
Abrupt threshold: the fraction of roots that reach the cap is < 0.1% for m_ef in {0.8, 0.9, 0.95} and > 5% for m_ef in {1.05, 1.2, 1.5}.
Critical cleanup: with m = 1.5, cleanup d = 0.30 (m_ef = 1.05) still has > 5% of roots reaching the cap, while d = 0.40 (m_ef = 0.9) has < 0.1% and a mean of executed jobs per root within 3% of 10.

Backlog after arrivals stop (service capacity 50 jobs/step, 5 roots/step for 200 steps): the backlog is empty 1,000 steps later in >= 99% of runs for m_ef in {0.8, 0.95}, and is larger than at the stop in >= 90% of runs for m_ef in {1.05, 1.2}.
Depth limit: with m = 1.5 and no cleanup, a maximum depth D bounds the mean executed jobs per root within 3% of (m^(D+1) - 1)/(m - 1) for D in {3, 5, 8} (8.1, 20.8, 74.9).

params.rules: Children per executed job ~ Poisson(m); each child is cancelled independently with probability d before running, so executed children ~ Poisson(m(1-d)). A generation of n jobs spawns Poisson(n*m_ef) executed children (lib Poisson: exact below mean 30, rounded normal approximation above). Backlog model: per step, Poisson(arrivals) roots arrive while t < arrival_steps; min(capacity, backlog) jobs run and spawn Poisson(run*m_ef) executed children.
